title: Last Moment Before Ants Fall
statement:
A wooden plank has length `n` units and lies along the number line from position `0` to position `n`. Some ants are walking on it. Every ant moves at a speed of one unit per second, either towards the left end or towards the right end, and each ant starts at its own integer position between `0` and `n`.

When two ants walking in opposite directions meet at the same point, both of them immediately turn around and keep walking in the opposite direction. Turning around takes no time. An ant falls off the plank the moment it reaches position `0` while walking left, or position `n` while walking right.

You are given the starting positions of the ants walking left and of the ants walking right. Return the time (in seconds) at which the last ant falls off the plank. An ant that starts at the end it is walking towards falls off at time `0`.
inputFormat:
The first line contains `n`.
The second line contains `a` followed by `a` integers: the starting positions of the ants walking left (the line is just `0` when there are none).
The third line contains `b` followed by `b` integers: the starting positions of the ants walking right (the line is just `0` when there are none).
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the time at which the last ant falls off the plank.
constraints: a, b ≥ 0 and 1 ≤ a + b ≤ min(n + 1, 10^5)
All starting positions are distinct (no two ants start at the same point, and no position appears in both lists)

examples.explanation: Without worrying about collisions: the left-walkers at 3 and 7 would fall at times 3 and 7, and the right-walkers at 2, 5, 9 would fall at times 8, 5, 1. The latest is 8. Collisions do not change the answer because two ants that turn around are the same as two ants that pass through each other.
Both ants walk right, so they never meet. The ant at 1 needs 4 seconds, the ant at 4 needs 1 second.

The ant at 7 walks left and the ant at 0 walks right; they meet in the middle after 3.5 seconds and bounce back, so the left-walker ends at 0 after 7 seconds and the right-walker ends at 7 after 7 seconds.

hints: Think about what a collision does to the set of positions the ants occupy at any moment. If two ants are exchanged for two identical ghosts that pass through each other, is anything different?
Since the ants are indistinguishable for the purpose of timing, a collision can be ignored: treat every ant as walking straight through the others.
An ant at position x walking left falls at time x, and one walking right falls at time n - x. The answer is the maximum over all ants.
